articleTitle: COHOMOLOGY OF BRAIDS, PRINCIPAL CONGRUENCE SUBGROUPS AND GEOMETRIC REPRESENTATIONS
abstract: The main purpose of this article is to give the integral cohomology of classical principal congruence subgroups in SL(2, ℤ) as well as their analogues in the 3-strand braid group with local coefficients in symmetric powers of the natural symplectic representation. The resulting answers (1) correspond to certain modular forms in characteristic zero and (2) the cohomology of certain spaces in homotopy theory in characteristic p. The torsion is given in terms of the structure of a ‘p-divided power algebra’.The work is an extension of the work in Callegaro et al. [The cohomology of the braid group B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and of SL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ) with coefficients in a geometric representation, Quart. J. Math. 64 (2013), 847–889] as well as extensions of a classical computation of Shimura to integral coefficients. The results here contrast the local coefficients such as that in Looijenga [Stable cohomology of the mapping class group with symplectic coefficients and of the universal Abel–Jacobi map, J. Algebraic Geom. 5 (1996), 135–150] and Tillmann [The representation of the mapping class group of a surface on its fundamental group in stable homology, Quart. J. Math. 61 (2010), 373–380].

articleTitle: FOLDING FREE-GROUP AUTOMORPHISMS
abstract: We describe an algorithm that uses Stallings' folding technique to decompose an element of Aut(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) as a product of Whitehead automorphisms (and hence as a product of Nielsen transformations). This algorithm is known to experts, but has not yet appeared in the literature. We use the algorithm to give an alternative method of finding a finite generating set for the subgroup of Aut(F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>) that fixes a subset Y of the basis elements, and the subgroup that fixes each element of Y up to conjugacy. We show that the intersection of this latter subgroup with I A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is also finitely generated.

articleTitle: ON CHAINS OF PRIME IDEALS IN RINGS OF SEMIALGEBRAIC FUNCTIONS
abstract: In this work, we study the structure of non-refinable chains of prime ideals in the (real closed) rings (M) and *(M) of semialgebraic and bounded semialgebraic functions on a semialgebraic set M⊂ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. We pay special attention to the prime z-ideals of (M) and the minimal prime ideals of both rings. For the last, a decomposition of each semialgebraic set as an irredundant finite union of closed pure dimensional semialgebraic subsets plays a crucial role. We prove moreover the existence of maximal ideals in the ring (M) of prefixed height whenever M is non-compact.

articleTitle: COARSE CLASSIFICATION OF ABELIAN GROUPS AND AMENABLE SHIFT-HOMOGENEOUS METRIC SPACES
abstract: We classify countable locally finite-by-abelian groups up to coarse isomorphism. Our classification is derived from a coarse classification of amenable shift-homogeneous metric spaces.

articleTitle: CONNECTEDNESS OF THE MODULI OF Sp(2p, 2q)-HIGGS BUNDLES
abstract: Using the Morse-theoretic techniques introduced by Hitchin, we prove that the moduli space of Sp(2p, 2q)-Higgs bundles over a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2 is connected. In particular, this implies that the moduli space of representations of the fundamental group of the surface in Sp(2p, 2q) is connected.

articleTitle: THE PRODUCT STRUCTURE OF THE EQUIVARIANT K-THEORY OF THE BASED LOOP GROUP OF SU(2)
abstract: Let G=SU(2) and let Ω G denote the space of continuous based loops in G, equipped with the pointwise conjugation action of G. It is a classical fact in topology that the ordinary cohomology H*(Ω G) is a divided polynomial algebra Γ[x]. The algebra Γ[x] can be described as an inverse limit as k→∞ of the symmetric subalgebra in Λ(x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>), where Λ(x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>) is the usual exterior algebra in the variables x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf>. We compute the R(G)-algebra structure of the G-equivariant K-theory K*<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>(Ω G) which naturally generalizes the classical computation of H*(Ω G) as Γ[x]. Specifically, we prove that K*<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>(Ω G) is an inverse limit of the symmetric (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf>-invariant) subalgebra (K*<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>((ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</sup>))<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">S</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf> of K*<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>((ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</sup>), where the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf> acts in the natural way on the factors of the product (ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</sup> and G acts diagonally via the standard action on each factor.

articleTitle: FUNCTOR CALCULUS AND THE DISCRIMINANT METHOD
abstract: The discriminant method is a tool for describing the cohomology, or the homotopy type, of certain spaces of smooth maps with uncomplicated singularities from a smooth compact manifold L to ℝ <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>. We recast some of it in the language of functor calculus. This reformulation allows us to use the discriminant method in a setting where we wish to impose conditions on the multilocal behavior of smooth maps f : L → ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>.

articleTitle: ON THE BRAUER GROUP OF DIAGONAL CUBIC SURFACES
abstract: We are concerned with finding explicit generators of the Brauer group of diagonal cubic surfaces in terms of norm residue symbols, which was originally studied by Manin. We introduce the notion of uniform generators and find that the Brauer group of some classes of diagonal cubic surfaces have uniform generators. However, we also prove that the Brauer group of general diagonal cubic surfaces do not have such ones. This reveals that a result of Manin for certain diagonal cubic surfaces cannot be generalized in some sense.

articleTitle: CHARACTER INJECTIVITY AND PROJECTIVITY OF BANACH MODULES
abstract: Let be a Banach algebra and let φ be a non-zero character on. We introduce and study the notions φ-injectivity and φ-projectivity for Banach-modules ℰ by modifying the injectivity and projectivity of ℰ. We give some necessary and sufficient conditions for φ-injectivity and φ-projectivity of ℰ. In sequel, we establish an important relationship between φ-amenability of and φ-injectivity of ℰ. This gives a positive answer to a question of Hellemskii in the setting of injectivity based on φ.

articleTitle: ON THE COMPLEXITY OF THE LIOUVILLE NUMBERS IN POSITIVE CHARACTERISTIC
abstract: We investigate the complexity of the set of Liouville numbers in the field of formal Laurent series in positive characteristic. In this setting, we prove some results analogous to those on the real numbers concerning the size and dimension of. In particular, we show that has Haar measure 0 and Hausdorff dimension 0. We locate the exact cut-point at which the h-dimensional Hausdorff measure of drops from infinity to zero for any dimension function h. Our results also include the fact that if has infinite h-dimensional Hausdorff measure, then it does not have σ-finite h-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

articleTitle: SHORT UNITRIANGULAR FACTORIZATIONS OF SL2(ℤ[1/p])
abstract: We prove that every matrix in SL <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(ℤ[1/p]) can be written as a product of at most five elementary matrices. This statement can also be interpreted in terms of short division chains in ℤ[1/p]. Similar bounds for the number of factors were known previously only under the generalized Riemann hypothesis.

articleTitle: EXPONENTIAL CONVERGENCE RATES OF SECOND QUANTIZATION SEMIGROUPS AND APPLICATIONS
abstract: Exponential convergence rates in the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-tail norm and entropy are characterized for the second quantization semigroups by using the corresponding base Dirichlet form. This supplements the well-known result on the L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-exponential convergence rate of second quantization semigroups. As applications, birth–death-type processes on Poisson spaces and the path space of Lévy processes are investigated.

articleTitle: NUMERICAL RADIUS OF RANK-1 OPERATORS ON BANACH SPACES
abstract: We study the rank-1 numerical index of a Banach space, namely the infimum of the numerical radii of those rank-1 operators on the space which have norm 1. We show that the rank-1 numerical index is always greater than or equal to 1/e. We also present properties of this index and some examples.

articleTitle: AN OUTER ADMISSIBLE ACTION OF A COMMUTATIVE LOCALLY COMPACT GROUP ON THE GENERIC DYNAMICS FACTOR
abstract: The generic dynamics factor is a small, monotone complete, hyperfinite wild factor of Type III obtained as a quotient of the Borel *-envelope of the Fermion algebra. In our earlier work with Wright, we constructed infinitely many outer actions of any Polish group equipped with a dense normal subgroup on. These results are algebraic and in another work with Wright, we constructed an outer admissible action of the additive group ℝ of real numbers and the torus on. Let G be any locally compact second countable commutative Hausdorff group. In this paper, we shall show that there exists an appropriate parameterization, for, that makes it possible to generalize the results of the works above, and to construct an admissible outer action of G on. When an action α of G on; is admissible, we can define the small monotone cross product <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> G and the dual action a of Ĝ in such a way that, the Takesaki's duality principle holds true and this is a new parameterization of the algebra.

articleTitle: CHIRAL ANOMALY VIA VERTEX ALGEBROIDS
abstract: The Riemann-Roch type formula for the chiral anomaly is “animated” as a morphims of appropriately defined gerbes.

articleTitle: ON WARING'S PROBLEM: TWO SQUARES, TWO CUBES AND TWO SIXTH POWERS
abstract: We investigate the number of representations of a large positive integer as the sum of two squares, two positive integral cubes and two sixth powers, showing that the anticipated asymptotic formula fails for at most O((log X)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+ε</sup>) positive integers not exceeding X.

articleTitle: BIFURCATION OF CLIFFORD TORI IN BERGER 3-SPHERES
abstract: We study the intrinsic and the extrinsic geometry of Clifford tori in Berger spheres <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathbb{T}_\tau^3,\tau}$</tex>, τ>0, and use these results to prove several local rigidity and bifurcation results in this context.

articleTitle: THE BISHOP–PHELPS–BOLLOBÁS PROPERTY FOR HERMITIAN FORMS ON HILBERT SPACES
abstract: In this paper, we prove that the Bishop–Phelps–Bollobás Theorem holds for hermitian forms on a complex Hilbert space and for symmetric bilinear forms on a real or complex Hilbert space. The Bishop–Phelps–Bollobás Theorem for operators in the Schatten–von Neumann classes is also obtained.

articleTitle: DIFFERENTIAL INCLUSIONS, NON-ABSOLUTELY CONVERGENT INTEGRALS AND THE FIRST THEOREM OF COMPLEX ANALYSIS
abstract: In the theory of complex-valued functions of a complex variable, arguably the first striking theorem is that pointwise differentiability implies C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup> regularity. As mentioned in Ahlfors [Complex Analysis. An Introduction to the Theory of Analytic Functions of One Complex Variable, 3rd edn, International Series in Pure and Applied Mathematics, McGraw-Hill Book Co., New York, 1978], there have been a number of studies [Porcelli and Connell, A proof of the power series expansion without Cauchy's formula, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 67 (1961), 177–181; Plunkett, A topological proof of the continuity of the derivative of a function of a complex variable, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 65 (1959), 1–4] proving this theorem without use of complex integration but at the cost of considerably more complexity. In this note, we will use the theory of non-absolutely convergent integrals to firstly give a very short proof of this result without complex integration, and secondly (in combination with some elements of the theory of elliptic regularity) provide a far reaching generalization.

articleTitle: ON VERY NON-LINEAR SUBSETS OF CONTINUOUS FUNCTIONS
abstract: In this paper, we continue the study initiated by Gurariy and Quarta in 2004 on the existence of linear spaces formed, up to the null vector, by continuous functions that attain the maximum only at one point. Inserting a topological flavor to the subject, we prove that results already known for functions defined on certain subsets of ℝ are actually true for functions on quite general topological spaces. In the line of the original results of Gurariy and Quarta, we prove that, depending on the desired dimension, such subspaces may exist or not.

articleTitle: LOCALIZATION AND HOMOLOGICAL STABILITY OF CONFIGURATION SPACES
abstract: Church [Homological stability for configuration spaces of manifolds, Invent. Math. 188 (2012), 465–504] used representation stability to prove that the space of configurations of distinct unordered points in a closed manifold exhibit rational homological stability. A second proof was also given by Randal-Williams [Homological stability for unordered configuration spaces, Q. J. Math. 64 (2013), 303–326] using transfer maps. We give a third proof of this fact using localization and rational homotopy theory. This gives new insight into the role that the rationals play in homological stability. Our methods also yield new information about stability for torsion in the homology of configuration spaces of points in a closed manifold.

articleTitle: OSCILLATORY PROPERTIES OF REAL FUNCTIONS WITH WEAKLY BOUNDED MELLIN TRANSFORM
abstract: We show that the error term of the counting function of sums of two squares has oscillations of logarithmic frequency and size x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>(log x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3/2−ε</sup>. We do that by showing a theorem on oscillations for error terms of a rather general class of real functions. If the Mellin transform of f(x) has a singularity at ρ=β+iγ, γ≠0, with the principal summand of the form (s−ρ)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−b</sup>(log(s−ρ))<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sup> h(s), h(ρ)≠0, we obtain oscillations of logarithmic frequency and size x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">β</sup>(log x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b−1−ε</sup>. We also apply this result to other arithmetical functions related to sums of two squares.

articleTitle: FAITHFUL ACTIONS ON COMMUTATIVE DIFFERENTIAL GRADED ALGEBRAS AND THE GROUP ISOMORPHISM PROBLEM
abstract: We prove that the isomorphism type of a large class of groups is determined by the class of differential graded algebras over an integral domain with mild conditions, on which these groups act faithfully.

articleTitle: A SIMPLE REMARK ON THE FIELD OF MODULI OF RATIONAL MAPS
abstract: A complex rational map R ∈ ℂ[z] has associated its field of moduli ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>, an invariant under conjugation by Möbius transformations, which is contained in every field of definition of R. In general, ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf> is not a field of definition of R as it is shown by explicit examples due to Silverman. In these examples, the rational maps are definable over a degree 2 extension of the field of moduli. In this paper, we observe that such a property always holds, that is, every rational map is definable over an extension of degree at most 2 of its field of moduli. The main ingredient in the proof is Weil's descent theorem, applied to the Riemann sphere, and the fact that the group of automorphisms of degree at least 2 rational maps are well known.

articleTitle: LARGE C*-ALGEBRAS OF UNIVERSALLY MEASURABLE OPERATORS
abstract: For a C*-algebra A, Pedersen defined the concept of universal measurability for self-adjoint elements of A**, the enveloping von Neumann algebra of A. Although he was unable to show that u, the set of universally measurable elements, is a Jordan algebra, he showed that; contains a large Jordan algebra, u;<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. We show by means of a 2;2 matrix trick that;<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is in fact the real part of a C*-algebra. If it is ever shown that is always a Jordan algebra, then the same trick will show that u; is the real part of a C*-algebra.

articleTitle: BIPARTITE GRAPHS AND QUASIPOSITIVE SURFACES
abstract: We present a simple combinatorial model for quasipositive surfaces and positive braids, based on embedded bipartite graphs. As a first application, we extend the well-known duality on standard diagrams of torus links to twisted torus links. We then introduce a combinatorial notion of adjacency for bipartite graph links and discuss its potential relation with the adjacency problem for plane curve singularities.

articleTitle: THE AUTOCORRELATION OF THE MÖBIUS FUNCTION AND CHOWLA'S CONJECTURE FOR THE RATIONAL FUNCTION FIELD
abstract: We prove a function field version of Chowla's conjecture on the autocorrelation of the Möbius function in the limit of a large finite field.

articleTitle: UNLIKELY INTERSECTIONS FOR CURVES IN MULTIPLICATIVE GROUPS OVER POSITIVE CHARACTERISTIC
abstract: The conjectures associated with the names of Zilber–Pink greatly generalize results associated with the names of Manin–Mumford and Mordell–Lang, but unlike the latter they are at present restricted to zero characteristic. We make a start on removing this restriction by stating a conjecture for curves in multiplicative groups over positive characteristic, and we verify the conjecture in three dimensions as well as for some special lines in general dimension. We also give an example where the finite set in question can be explicitly determined.

articleTitle: KO-THEORY OF COMPLEX PARTIAL FLAG MANIFOLDS
abstract: The KO-groups of the complex partial flag manifold U(n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>+⋯+n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf>)/U(n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>)×⋯×U(n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ℓ</inf>) are determined by the Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence.

articleTitle: ON THE AMICK–FRAENKEL CONJECTURE
abstract: In 1987, C. J. Amick and L. E. Fraenkel published a paper on the behaviour of the Stokes wave of extreme form near its crest, where they obtained a complete asymptotic expansion for the angle between the wave profile and the horizontal. Their derivation of the expansion relied on an assumption of linear independence over the rationals of solutions of a certain transcendental equation, which is still an open question. We show that Schanuel's conjecture implies not only the conjectured linear independence of solutions, but also their algebraic independence.

articleTitle: A RECURSION FORMULA FOR MOMENTS OF DERIVATIVES OF RANDOM MATRIX POLYNOMIALS
abstract: We give asymptotic formulae for random matrix averages of derivatives of characteristic polynomials over the groups USp(2N), SO(2N) and O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>(2N). These averages are used to predict the asymptotic formulae for moments of derivatives of L-functions which arise in number theory. Each formula gives the leading constant of the asymptotic in terms of determinants of hypergeometric functions. We find a differential recurrence relation between these determinants that allows the rapid computation of the (k+1)st constant in terms of the kth and (k−1)st. This recurrence is reminiscent of a Toda lattice equation arising in the theory of τ-functions associated with Painlevé differential equations.

articleTitle: STOPPING THE CCR FLOW AND ITS ISOMETRIC COCYCLES
abstract: It is shown how to use non-commutative stopping times in order to stop the CCR flow of arbitrary index and also its isometric cocycles, i.e. left operator Markovian cocycles on Boson Fock space. Stopping the CCR flow yields a homomorphism from the semigroup of stopping times, equipped with the convolution product, into the semigroup of unital endomorphisms of the von Neumann algebra of bounded operators on the ambient Fock space. The operators produced by stopping cocycles themselves satisfy a cocycle relation.

articleTitle: ON THE STEINHAUS TILING PROBLEM FOR ℤ3
abstract: Steinhaus asked in the 1950s whether there exists a set in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> meeting every isometric copy of ℤ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in precisely one point. Such a ‘Steinhaus set’ was constructed by Jackson and Mauldin. What about ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>? Is there a subset S of ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> meeting every isometric copy of ℤ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in exactly one point? We offer heuristic evidence that the answer is ‘no’.

articleTitle: EXACT COVERING SYSTEMS IN NUMBER FIELDS
abstract: It is well known that, in an exact covering system in ℤ, the biggest modulus must be repeated. Very recently, Kim gave an analogous result for certain quadratic fields, and Kim also conjectured that it must hold in any algebraic number field. In this paper, we prove Kim's conjecture. In other words, we prove that exact covering systems in any algebraic number field must have repeated moduli.

articleTitle: THE DISTRIBUTION OF THE LOGARITHMIC DERIVATIVE OF THE RIEMANN ZETA-FUNCTION
abstract: We investigate the distribution of the logarithmic derivative of the Riemann zeta-function on the line ℜ(s)=σ, where σ lies in a certain range near the critical line σ=½. For such σ, we show that the distribution of ζ′/ζ(s) converges to a two-dimensional Gaussian distribution in the complex plane. Upper bounds on the rate of convergence to the Gaussian distribution are also obtained.

articleTitle: EFFECTIVE PRIME IDEAL THEOREM AND EXPONENTS OF IDEAL CLASS GROUPS
abstract: For a family of G-fields K, we show an effective prime ideal theorem with probability 1. Namely, outside a density zero set, π(x, K)=Li(x)+O(x/(log x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) for x≥(log d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sup> for some c depending on G. Using the effective prime ideal theorem, we show that the exponents e<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> of the ideal class groups of a family of G-fields increase along with d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> with probability 1.

articleTitle: FROM PRIMITIVE SPACES OF BOUNDED RANK MATRICES TO A GENERALIZED GERSTENHABER THEOREM
abstract: A recent generalization of Gerstenhaber's theorem on spaces of nilpotent matrices is derived, under mild conditions on the cardinality of the underlying field, from Atkinson's structure theorem on primitive spaces of bounded rank matrices.

articleTitle: SIMPLE ZEROS OF PRIMITIVE DIRICHLET L-FUNCTIONS AND THE ASYMPTOTIC LARGE SIEVE
abstract: Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis, we show using the asymptotic large sieve that 91% of the zeros of primitive Dirichlet L-functions are simple. This improves on earlier work of Özlük which gives a proportion of at most 86%. We further compute the q-analogue of the Pair Correlation Function F(α) averaged over all primitive Dirichlet L-functions in the range |α| < 2. Previously such a result was available only when the average included all the characters χ. As a corollary of our results, we obtain an asymptotic formula for a sum over characters similar to the one encountered in the Barban–Davenport–Halberstam Theorem.

articleTitle: PRIMES IN ARITHMETIC PROGRESSIONS TO SPACED MODULI. II
A CLASS OF INCOMPLETE CHARACTER SUMS
abstract: Using ℓ-adic cohomology of tensor inductions of lisse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$</tex>-sheaves, we study a class of incomplete character sums.

articleTitle: ATOMIC DECOMPOSITIONS, DUAL SPACES AND INTERPOLATIONS OF MARTINGALE HARDY–LORENTZ–KARAMATA SPACES
abstract: We introduce the martingale Hardy–Lorentz–Karamata spaces. The atomic decompositions of these martingale function spaces are established. The dual spaces are identified and some interpolation properties of the martingale Hardy–Lorentz–Karamata spaces are obtained.

articleTitle: BOUNDARIES FOR STRONG SCHUR SPACES
abstract: It is known that if a Banach space X does not contain an isomorphic copy of c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, then for any boundary B and representation B = ∪<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n=1</inf> B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> such that the sequence B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is increasing, there exist an index m and some r>0 such that B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> is r-norming for X. In this note, we show that if some B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> is uniformly norming, that is, there exists r>0 not depending on a boundary B and a representation B= ∪ B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, then that property characterizes Strong Schur spaces.

articleTitle: ITERATED FIBRE SUMS OF ALGEBRAIC LEFSCHETZ FIBRATIONS
abstract: Let M denote the total space of a Lefschetz fibration, obtained by blowing up a Lefschetz pencil on an algebraic surface. We consider the n-fold fibre sum M(n), generalizing the construction of the elliptic surfaces E(n). For a Lefschetz pencil on a simply connected minimal surface of general type, we partially calculate the Seiberg–Witten invariants of the fibre sum M(n) using a formula of Morgan–Szabó–Taubes. As an application, we derive an obstruction for self-diffeomorphisms of the boundary of the tubular neighbourhood of a general fibre in M(n) to extend over the complement of the neighbourhood. Similar obstructions are known in the case of elliptic surfaces.

articleTitle: A CHAIN CONDITION FOR OPERATORS FROM C(K)-SPACES
abstract: We introduce a chain condition, defined for operators acting on C(K)-spaces, which is intermediate between weak compactness and having weakly compactly generated range. It is motivated by Pełczyński's characterization of weakly compact operators on C(K)-spaces. We prove that if K is extremally disconnected and X is a Banach space, then, for an operator T : C(K)→X, T is weakly compact if and only if T satisfies if and only if the representing vector measure of T satisfies an analogous chain condition. As a tool for proving the above-mentioned result, we derive a topological counterpart of Rosenthal's lemma. We exhibit several compact Hausdorff spaces K for which the identity operator on C(K) satisfies, for example, both locally connected compact spaces having countable cellularity and ladder system spaces have this property. Using a Ramsey-type theorem, due to Dushnik and Miller, we prove that the collection of operators on a C(K)-space satisfying forms a closed left ideal of ℬ(C(K)).

articleTitle: CLASSIFICATION OF CONGRUENCES FOR MOCK THETA FUNCTIONS AND WEAKLY HOLOMORPHIC MODULAR FORMS
abstract: Let f(q) denote Ramanujan's mock theta function It is known that there are many linear congruences for the coefficients of f(q) and other mock theta functions. We prove that if the linear congruence a(mn+t) ≡ 0 (mod ℓ) holds for some prime ℓ ≥ 5, then ℓ|m and ((24t − 1)/ℓ) ≠ (−1/ℓ). We prove analogous results for the mock theta function ω(q) and for a large class of weakly holomorphic modular forms which includes η-quotients. This extends work of Radu, in which he proves a conjecture of Ahlgren and Ono for the partition function p(n).

articleTitle: SMOOTH APPROXIMATIONS OF NORMS IN SEPARABLE BANACH SPACES
abstract: Let X be a separable real Banach space having a k-times continuously Fréchet differentiable (i.e. C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>-smooth) norm where k∈{1, …, ∞}. We show that any equivalent norm on X can be approximated uniformly on bounded sets by C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</sup>-smooth norms.

articleTitle: THE STRONG ARTIN CONJECTURE AND LARGE CLASS NUMBERS
abstract: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) and the Artin conjecture for Artin L-functions, Duke found an upper bound of the class number of a totally real field of degree n whose normal closure is an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> Galois extension over ℚ. Again under the GRH and the Artin conjecture, he constructed totally real number fields whose Galois closures are S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> with the largest possible class numbers up to a constant. We prove that the strong Artin conjecture is enough to obtain Duke's result. Moreover, we prove the strong Artin conjecture for S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> Galois extensions; hence the case n=4 is unconditional.

articleTitle: ON SERIES OF DILATED FUNCTIONS
abstract: Given a periodic function f, we study the almost everywhere and norm convergence of series <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}ck f(kx)}$</tex>. As the classical theory shows, the behavior of such series is determined by a combination of analytic and number theoretic factors, but precise results exist only in a few special cases. In this paper, we use connections with orthogonal function theory and greatest common divisor sums to prove several new results and improve old ones, and also to simplify and unify the theory.

articleTitle: SPECTRAL SYNTHESIS IN THE MULTIPLIER ALGEBRA OF A C0(X)-ALGEBRA
abstract: Let A be a C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(X)-algebra with continuous map φ from Prim(A), the primitive ideal space of A, to a locally compact Hausdorff space X. Then the multiplier algebra M(A) is a C(β X)-algebra with continuous map <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\phi}$</tex>: Prim(M(A)) → β X extending φ. For x ∈ Im(φ), let J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> = ⋂{P ∈ Prim(A): φ(P) = x} and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Hx=\cap Q\epsilon Prim (M(A)):\phi(Q)=x.ThenJx\subseteq Hx\subseteq Jx,$</tex>, the strict closure of J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> in M(A). Thus, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is strictly closed if and only if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${Hx=Jx}$</tex>, and the ‘spectral synthesis’ question asks when this happens. In this paper, it is shown that, for σ-unital A, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is strictly closed for all x ∈ Im(φ) if and only if J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> is locally modular for all x ∈ Im(φ) and φ is a closed map relative to its image. Various related results are obtained.

articleTitle: SLICING CORANK 1 MAP GERMS FROM ℂ2 TO ℂ3
abstract: The classification and the geometry of corank 1 map germs f:(ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 0)→(ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, 0) have been studied by David Mond. Normal forms of such maps f(x, y)=(x, p(x, y), q(x, y)) suggest, at least in some cases, that they could be seen as 1-parameter unfoldings of the plane curves γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>(y)=(p(x, y), q(x, y)). If a certain genericity condition is satisfied, then the transverse slice curve γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> contains information on the geometry of f. We introduce invariants C, J, T related to the Reidemeister moves (codimension 1 transitions) that appear in a stable perturbation of γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. We compare them with Mond's invariants of f and obtain interesting geometric results. For instance, f is finitely determined if and only if C, J, T<∞ and given a 1-parameter family f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf>, it is Whitney equisingular if and only if the three invariants are independent of t.

articleTitle: INVARIANT LAMINATIONS FOR IRREDUCIBLE AUTOMORPHISMS OF FREE GROUPS
abstract: For every irreducible hyperbolic automorphism φ of F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> (i.e. the analog of a pseudo-Anosov mapping class) it is shown that the algebraic lamination dual to the forward limit tree T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</inf>(φ) is obtained as ‘diagonal closure’ of the support of the backward limit current μ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</inf>(φ). This diagonal closure is obtained through a finite procedure analogous to adding diagonal leaves from the complementary components to the stable lamination of a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism. We also give several new characterizations as well as a structure theorem for the dual lamination of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</inf>(φ), in terms of Bestvina–Feighn–Handel's ‘stable lamination’ associated to φ.

articleTitle: ON HOMOGENEOUS RICCI SOLITONS
abstract: We study the evolution of homogeneous Ricci solitons under the bracket flow, a dynamical system on the space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${H_{q,n}\subset\triangle^{2} \cal {g}^*\otimes \cal g}$</tex> of all homogeneous spaces of dimension n with a q-dimensional isotropy, which is equivalent to the Ricci flow for homogeneous manifolds. We prove that algebraic solitons (i.e. the Ricci operator is a multiple of the identity plus a derivation) are precisely the fixed points of the system, and that a homogeneous Ricci soliton is isometric to an algebraic soliton if and only if the corresponding bracket flow solution is not chaotic, in the sense that its ω-limit set consists of a single point. We also geometrically characterize algebraic solitons among homogeneous Ricci solitons as those for which the Ricci flow solution is simultaneously diagonalizable.

articleTitle: LINEAR ISOMETRIES BETWEEN REAL JB*-TRIPLES AND C*-ALGEBRAS
abstract: Let T: A→B be a (not necessarily surjective) linear isometry between two real JB*-triples. Then for each a∈A, there exists a tripotent u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> in the bidual, B″, of B such that {u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, T({f, g, h}), u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>}={u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, {T(f), T(g), T(h)}, u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>}, for all f, g, h in the real JB*-subtriple, A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, generated by a; the mapping {u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>, T(·), u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>}:A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>→B″ is a linear isometry. Furthermore, when B is a real C*-algebra, the projection p=p<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>=u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup> u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> satisfies that T(·)p:A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>→B″ is an isometric triple homomorphism. When A and B are real C*-algebras and A is abelian of real type, then there exists a partial isometry u∈B″ such that the mapping T(·)u*u:A→B″ is an isometric triple homomorphism. These results generalize, to the real setting, some previous contributions due to Chu and Wong, and Chu and Mackey in 2004 and 2005. We give an example of a non-surjective real linear isometry which cannot be complexified to a complex isometry, showing that the results in the real setting cannot be derived by a mere complexification argument.

articleTitle: A CHARACTERIZATION OF UNIFORM PRO-p GROUPS
abstract: In the present paper, we propose and supply evidence for the following conjecture, aimed at characterizing uniform pro-p groups. Suppose that p≥3 and let G be a torsion-free pro-p group of finite rank. Then G is uniform if and only if its minimal number of generators is equal to the dimension of G as a p-adic manifold, i.e. d(G) = dim(G). In particular, we prove that the assertion is true whenever G is soluble or p > dim(G).

articleTitle: CONSTRUCTING CO-HIGGS BUNDLES ON ℂℙ2
abstract: On a complex manifold, a co-Higgs bundle is a holomorphic vector bundle with an endomorphism twisted by the tangent bundle. The notion of generalized holomorphic bundle in Hitchin's generalized geometry coincides with that of co-Higgs bundle when the generalized complex manifold is ordinary complex. Schwarzenberger's rank-2 vector bundle on the projective plane, constructed from a line bundle on the double cover ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>×ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>→ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, is naturally a co-Higgs bundle, with the twisted endomorphism, or ‘Higgs field’, also descending from the double cover. Allowing the branch conic to vary, we find that Schwarzenberger bundles give rise to an eight-dimensional moduli space of co-Higgs bundles. After studying the deformation theory for co-Higgs bundles on complex manifolds, we conclude that a co-Higgs bundle arising from a Schwarzenberger bundle with non-zero Higgs field is rigid, in the sense that a nearby deformation is again Schwarzenberger.

articleTitle: POSITIVELY NORMING SETS IN BANACH FUNCTION SPACES
abstract: The notion of positively norming set, a specific definition of norming type sets for Banach lattices, is analyzed. We show that the size of positively norming sets (in terms of compactness and order boundedness) is directly related to the existence of lattice copies of L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-spaces. As an application, we provide a version of Kadec–Pełczyński's dichotomy for order continuous Banach function spaces. A general description of positively norming sets using vector measure integration is also given.

articleTitle: STRATIFICATIONS ASSOCIATED TO REDUCTIVE GROUP ACTIONS ON AFFINE SPACES
abstract: For a complex reductive group G acting linearly on a complex affine space V with respect to a character ρ, we show two stratifications of V associated to this action (and a choice of invariant inner product on the Lie algebra of the maximal compact subgroup of G) coincide. The first is Hesselink's stratification by adapted 1-parameter subgroups and the second is the Morse theoretic stratification associated to the norm square of the moment map. We also give a proof of a version of the Kempf–Ness theorem, which states that the geometric invariant theory quotient is homeomorphic to the symplectic reduction (both taken with respect to ρ). Finally, for the space of representations of a quiver of fixed dimension, we show that the Morse theoretic stratification and Hesselink's stratification coincide with the stratification by Harder–Narasimhan types.

articleTitle: IMAGES OF GOLOD–SHAFAREVICH ALGEBRAS WITH SMALL GROWTH
abstract: We show that Golod–Shafarevich algebras can be homomorphically mapped onto infinite dimensional algebras with polynomial growth when mild assumptions about the number of relations of given degrees are introduced. This answers a question by Zel′manov. In the case where these algebras are finitely presented, we show that they can be mapped onto infinite-dimensional algebras with at most quadratic growth. We then use an elementary construction to show that any sufficiently regular function ≳ n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">log n</sup> may occur as the growth function of an algebra.

articleTitle: EINSTEIN MANIFOLDS WITH SKEW TORSION
abstract: This paper is devoted to the first systematic investigation of manifolds that are Einstein for a connection ∇ with skew-symmetric torsion. We derive the Einstein equation from a variational principle and prove that, for parallel torsion, any Einstein manifold with skew torsion has constant scalar curvature; and if it is complete of positive scalar ∇-curvature, it is necessarily compact and it has finite first fundamental group π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>. The longest part of the paper is devoted to the systematic construction of large families of examples. We discuss when a Riemannian Einstein manifold can be Einstein with skew torsion. We give examples of almost Hermitian, almost metric contact, and G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> manifolds that are Einstein with skew torsion. For example, we prove that any Einstein–Sasaki manifold and any seven-dimensional 3-Sasakian manifolds admit deformations into an Einstein metric with parallel skew torsion.

articleTitle: MONOTONICITY FORMULAE, VANISHING THEOREMS AND SOME GEOMETRIC APPLICATIONS
abstract: Using the stress-energy tensor, we establish some monotonicity formulae for vector bundle-valued p-forms satisfying the conservation law, provided that the base Riemannian (resp. Kähler) manifolds possess some real (resp. complex) p-exhaustion functions. Vanishing theorems follow immediately from the monotonicity formulae under suitable growth conditions on the energy of the p-forms. As an application, we establish a monotonicity formula for the Ricci form of a Kähler manifold of constant scalar curvature, and then get a growth condition to derive the Ricci flatness of the Kähler manifold. In particular, when the curvature does not change sign, the Kähler manifold is isometrically biholomorphic to C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>. Another application is to deduce the monotonicity formulae for volumes of minimal submanifolds in some outer spaces with suitable exhaustion functions. In this way, we recapture the classical volume monotonicity formulae of minimal submanifolds in Euclidean spaces. We also apply the vanishing theorems to Bernstein-type problem of submanifolds in Euclidean spaces with parallel mean curvature. In particular, we may obtain Bernstein-type results for minimal submanifolds, especially for minimal real Kähler submanifolds under weaker conditions.

articleTitle: OPEN BOOKS AND THE WEINSTEIN CONJECTURE
abstract: We show the existence of a contractible periodic Reeb orbit for any contact structure supported by an open book whose binding can be realized as a hypersurface of restricted contact type in a subcritical Stein manifold. A key ingredient in the proof is a higher dimensional version of Eliashberg's theorem about symplectic cobordisms from a contact manifold to a symplectic fibration.

articleTitle: MORSE THEORY WITH THE NORM-SQUARE OF A HYPERKÄHLER MOMENT MAP
abstract: We prove that the norm-square of a moment map associated to a linear action of a compact group on an affine variety satisfies a certain gradient inequality. This allows us to bound the gradient flow, even if we do not assume that the moment map is proper. We describe how this inequality can be extended to hyperkähler moment maps in some cases, and use Morse theory with the norm-squares of hyperkähler moment maps to compute the Betti numbers and cohomology rings of toric hyperkähler orbifolds.

articleTitle: IS THE MISSING AXIOM OF MATROID THEORY LOST FOREVER?
abstract: We conjecture that it is not possible to finitely axiomatize matroid representability in monadic second-order logic (MSOL) for matroids, and we describe some partial progress towards this conjecture. We present a collection of sentences in MSOL and show that it is possible to finitely axiomatize matroids using only sentences in this collection. Moreover, we can also axiomatize representability over any fixed finite field (assuming Rota's conjecture holds). We prove that it is not possible to finitely axiomatize representability, or representability over any fixed infinite field, using sentences from the collection.

articleTitle: EXTENDED SOLUTIONS OF THE HARMONIC MAP EQUATION IN THE SPECIAL UNITARY GROUP
abstract: We classify all harmonic maps of finite uniton number from a Riemann surface into SU (n) in terms of certain pieces of the Bruhat decomposition of Ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">alg</inf> SU (n), the subgroup of algebraic loops in SU (n). We give a description of the ‘Frenet frame data’ for such harmonic maps in a given class.

articleTitle: ON THE REPRESENTATION THEORY OF PARTIAL BRAUER ALGEBRAS
abstract: In this paper, we study the partial Brauer ℂ-algebras ℜ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(δ, δ′), where n∈ℕ and δ, δ′∈ℂ. We show that these algebras are generically semisimple, construct the Specht modules and determine the Specht module restriction rules for the restriction ℜ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n−1</inf> ↪ ℜ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. We also determine the corresponding decomposition matrix and the Cartan decomposition matrix.

articleTitle: SMOOTH MODULI SPACES OF ASSOCIATIVE SUBMANIFOLDS
abstract: Let M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> be a smooth manifold equipped with a G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-structure ϕ, and Y<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> be a closed compact ϕ-associative submanifold. McLean [Deformations of calibrated submanifolds, Comm. Anal. Geom. 6 (1998), 705–747] proved that the moduli space ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y, ϕ</inf> of the ϕ-associative deformations of Y has vanishing virtual dimension. In this paper, we perturb ϕ into a G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-structure ψ in order to ensure the smoothness of ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y, ψ</inf> near Y. If Y is allowed to have a boundary moving in a fixed coassociative submanifold X, it was proved in Gayet and Witt [Deformations of associative submanifolds with boundary, Adv. Math. 226 (2011), 2351–2370] that the moduli space ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y, X</inf> of the associative deformations of Y with boundary in X has finite virtual dimension. We show here that a generic perturbation of the boundary condition X into X′ gives the smoothness of ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y, X′</inf>. In another direction, we use Bochner's technique to prove a vanishing theorem that forces ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y</inf> or ℳ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Y, X</inf> to be smooth near Y. For every case, some explicit families of examples will be given.

articleTitle: GAIN OF REGULARITY FOR A BENNEY–LIN EQUATION TYPE
abstract: We study the existence of local and global solutions, the gain of regularity for the initial value problem associated to the Benney–Lin equation type perturbed by a dispersive and dissipative terms which appear in several fluids dynamics problems.

articleTitle: CLIFFORD–WOLF TRANSLATIONS OF LEFT INVARIANT RANDERS METRICS ON COMPACT LIE GROUPS
abstract: A Clifford–Wolf translation (CW-translation) of a connected Finsler space is an isometry which moves all points the same distance. A Finsler space (M, F) is called Clifford–Wolf homogeneous (CW-homogeneous) if, for any two points x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> ∈ M, there is a CW-translation ρ such that ρ(x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>) = x<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In this paper, we study CW-translations of left invariant Randers metrics on compact Lie groups. The main result is that a left invariant Randers metric on a compact, connected, simple Lie group is CW-homogeneous if and only if the indicatrix of the metric is a round sphere (not necessarily centered at the origin) with respect to a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. This presents a large number of examples of non-reversible Finsler metrics which are CW-homogeneous.

articleTitle: SUBDIRECT PRODUCTS OF GROUPS AND THE n-(n + 1)-(n + 2) CONJECTURE
abstract: We analyse the subgroup structure of direct products of groups. In particular, we seek to relate the finiteness properties of a subgroup to the way it is embedded in the ambient product. The titular conjecture gives a precise criterion for determining the finiteness properties of a fibre product of groups. Using a variety of approaches to this conjecture, we prove a general result on finite generation of homology groups of fibre products as well as results on the stronger finiteness properties F<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> and FP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, in certain special cases. As a consequence, we make progress on a conjectured characterization on higher finiteness conditions of a subgroup of a direct product of free or limit groups in terms of an embedding condition.

articleTitle: METABELIAN SL(N, ℂ) REPRESENTATIONS OF KNOT GROUPS, III: DEFORMATIONS
abstract: Given a knot K with complement N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf> and an irreducible metabelian SL(n, ℂ) representation α : π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>)→SL(n, ℂ), we establish the inequality dim H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>; sl(n, ℂ)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Adα</inf>)≥n−1. In the case of equality, we prove that α must have finite image and is conjugate to an SU(n) representation. In this case, we show α determines a smooth point ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> in the SL(n, ℂ) character variety, and we use a deformation argument to establish the existence of a smooth (n−1)-dimensional family of characters of irreducible SL(n, ℂ) representations near ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> and a corresponding subfamily of characters of irreducible SU(n) representations of real dimension n−1. Both families can be chosen so that ξ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> is the only metabelian character. Combining this with our previous existence results, we deduce the existence of large families of irreducible SU(n) and SL(n, ℂ) non-metabelian representation for knots K in homology 3-spheres Σ with non-trivial Alexander polynomial. We then relate the condition on twisted cohomology to a more accessible condition on untwisted cohomology of a certain metabelian branched cover <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{\sum}$</tex> of Σ branched along K.

articleTitle: GRAHAM HIGMAN'S LECTURES ON JANUARIALS
abstract: This is an account of a series of lectures of Graham Higman on januarials, namely coset graphs for actions of triangle groups which become 2-face maps when embedded in orientable surfaces.

articleTitle: LIMITING DISTRIBUTIONS OF THE CLASSICAL ERROR TERMS OF PRIME NUMBER THEORY
abstract: In this article, we prove a general theorem which establishes the existence of limiting distributions for a wide class of error terms from prime number theory. As a corollary to our main theorem, we deduce previous results of Wintner [On the asymptotic distribution of the remainder term of the prime number theorem, Amer. J. Math. 57 (1935), 534–538], Rubinstein and Sarnak [Chebyshev's bias, Experiment. Math. 3 (1994), 173–197] and of Ng [The summatory function of the Möbius function, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) 89 (2004), 361–389]. In addition, we establish limiting distribution results for the error term in the prime number theorem for an automorphic L-function, weighted sums of the Möbius function, weighted sums of the Liouville function, the sum of the Möbius function in an arithmetic progression and the error term in Chebotarev's density theorem.

articleTitle: FREE CENTRE-BY-METABELIAN LIE RINGS
abstract: We study the free centre-by-metabelian Lie ring, that is, the free Lie ring with the property that the second derived ideal is contained in the centre. We exhibit explicit generating sets for the homogeneous and fine homogeneous components of the second derived ideal. Each of these components is a direct sum of a free abelian group and a (possibly trivial) elementary abelian 2-group. Our generating sets are such that some of their elements generate the torsion subgroup while the remaining ones freely generate a free abelian group. A key ingredient of our approach is the determination of the dimensions of the corresponding homogeneous and fine homogeneous components of the free centre-by-metabelian Lie algebra over fields of characteristic other than 2. For that we exploit a six-term exact sequence of modules over a polynomial ring that is originally defined over the integers, but turns into a sequence whose terms are projective modules after tensoring with a suitable field. Our results correct a partly erroneous theorem in the literature.

articleTitle: ON FINITE UNIPOTENT TRANSVECTION GROUPS AND THEIR INVARIANTS
abstract: Let F be a field and V be a finite-dimensional F-vector space. A transvection is a unipotent pseudo-reflection in GL(V) and a transvection group is a linear group generated by transvections. Motivated by questions from modular invariant theory, we are investigating structural properties of finite and, mostly unipotent, transvection groups. Owing to a classical result of Serre, the ring of invariants of a finite linear group can only be a polynomial ring if the group is generated by pseudo-reflections that, in the case of p-groups in characteristic p, implies that the group is a transvection group. The converse of Serre's theorem is known to be false already in the case of elementary abelian groups. It is however true for extraspecial groups in characteristic p, as we show by describing all their faithful transvection representations. We generalize this result, proving that a finite group has a polynomial ring of invariants whenever it is a transvection p-group of nilpotence class≤2 with one-dimensional fixed point spaces on V and the dual V*. Along the way we prove several results, for example about the commutator structure of transvections, that will be useful in the analysis of more general classes of groups.

articleTitle: ERROR TERM IMPROVEMENTS FOR VAN DER CORPUT TRANSFORMS
abstract: We improve the error term in the van der Corput transform for exponential sums, ∑<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a≤n≤b</inf> g(n) exp(2π i f(n)). For many functions g and f, we can extract a simple explicit main term for the error. In addition, the methods of this paper avoid the use of the truncated Poisson formula, and thus can be applied to much longer intervals [a, b] with better estimates than previous results. As a result of these refinements, we are able to provide an improvement to the classical Kusmin–Landau inequality.
